messages.subject: Changing colors based on factor using small_multiple in ggplot2
parts:
Im graphing coefficients from multiple models for 2 species of birds using small_multiple in ggplot but I'd like to have the dot and whiskers color coded based on species. Currently all dot and whiskers are the same color.


# Generate a 'small multiple' plot
library(dotwhisker)
library(broom)
library (ggplot2)
small_multiple(m123456_df_speciesfor) + 
  theme_bw() + theme(axis.title.x=element_blank(),
      axis.text.x=element_blank(),
      axis.ticks.x=element_blank())+ylab("Coefficient estimate") +
geom_hline(yintercept = 0, colour = "grey60", linetype = 2) + 
ggtitle("Shrubland Bird") +

Bryan, 

colour was hardcoded in the function to "submodel", which you weren't using. 

I made a new version of the function that hard codes it to "Species". Ideally, you could submit a feature request to the dotwhisker maintainer to change this and be able to pass a colour argument through to the ggplot call. 

 library(dotwhisker)
library(broom)
library(tidyverse)

m123456_df_speciesfor <- read_csv("/Users/brandonhurr/Downloads/m123456_df_speciesfora.csv") %>% select(-X1)


small_multiple_test <- function (x, dodge_size = 0.4, show_intercept = FALSE, by_2sd = TRUE, 
          dot_args = list(size = 0.3), ...) 
{
  df <- dotwhisker:::dw_tidy(x, by_2sd = by_2sd, ...)
  if (!show_intercept) 
    df <- df %>% filter(!grepl("^\\(Intercept\\)$|^\\w+\\|\\w+$", 
                               term))
  term <- estimate <- model <- submodel <- conf.high <- conf.low <- NULL
  n_vars <- length(unique(df$term))
  if (!"model" %in% names(df)) {
    if (length(df$term) == n_vars) {
      stop("'Small multiple' plots are used to compare results across many different models; please submit results from more than one model")
    }
